lots.what_it_is: Ryllton Viney (b. 1944, Tasmanian printmaker), 'Courtyard, Provence No.1', unique state collagraph on Magnani paper, 2012, in a pine frame with white mat. Handwritten label reads 'Ryllton Viney / Courtyard, Provence No.1 / unique state collagraph on Magnani paper / 54 x 44' plus stock number 4284.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: no sold, unsold or asking prices found for this artist. Researcher reported no entries; my own WebSearch and Gowans API checks (viney, tyson) also found none. Artist has essentially no public auction record.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep and flip maximums are 0. The 4284 on the label is a gallery stock number, not a price. Premium 22% would apply to any hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: Label read clearly, but no priced evidence of any kind; signature on the sheet is a scrawl I cannot read on its own.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop (researcher submitted no entries).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 label read: 'Ryllton Viney', 'Courtyard, Provence No.1', 'Unique state collagraph on Magnani paper', '54 x 44', stock no. 4284 in marker. Under the 4284 there is a faint pencil figure (possibly a crossed-out old gallery price) that I cannot read reliably after enlarging, so it is not used. Photo 2: sheet signed lower left in pencil (illegible scrawl) and dated 2012 lower right. Image is small within a large mat, dark grey with ochre swirls. Pine frame looks sound, glazing intact in photos.
lots.condition: Appears clean, no visible foxing or damage in the photos; mat and frame look good. Glass reflections hide fine detail.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the image sheet foxed, faded or stuck down to the mat, and is there any gallery sticker or certificate on the back?

lots.guide_summary: Recent (last 24 months) same-artist full-size watercolours: 5 SOLD at $260 to $350 (Lawsons x2, Colville x2, Leski), plus 2 UNSOLD/passed in with last bids of $140 and $150. Guide $140 to $350, mostly sold evidence, no asking prices. All AUD, no conversion. Invaluable does not say whether priceResult includes premium.
lots.working: Keep: lowest recent comparable full-size SOLD = $260 (Leski, May 2026). 260 / 1.22 = 213.1, round down to $210 hammer ($256 all-in). The $80 Amanda Addams result is excluded (smaller 19 x 44 cm work, ambiguous record). Flip: likely resale about $300 hammer at a Tasmanian room (Colville x2 at $300). Less about 15% vendor commission ($45) and about $10 listing/photo fee, no outbound postage (consign locally) = $245 net. 245 / 2.44 = 100.4, round down to $100 hammer. Two passed-in results at $140 to $150 show resale is not assured.
lots.confidence_reason: Signature 'Geoff Tyson' read in an enlarged crop and the biography on the back matches; 5 recent sold results opened and parsed, but all come through one aggregator page with premium inclusion unknown, sizes and condition of this lot unverified, and passed-in results show patchy demand.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All 12 researcher entries matched the Invaluable JSON I fetched (titles, dates, priceResult, estimates). Gowans 2010 'Tea Trees Lagoon Bay' $130 omitted from my lists as too old (16 years) to be meaningful, not because it was wrong. The 2019, 2021 and 2017 entries are kept as category guide only. Also noted on the page but not used: Crow's (UK) 2017 GBP 38 small 10 inch work; Colville 2016 passed-in records.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop of lower right shows 'Geoff Tyson' signature in brush/pencil. Photo 3: handwritten biography on tissue paper on the backing: 'Geoffrey Tyson, born Launceston 3 April 1911, died 1986...' consistent with known facts. No date visible on the front. Subject is a white Georgian church with Doric portico and cupola tower, gums and gravestones; plausibly St Andrew's, Evandale (my guess). Image looks roughly 35 x 55 cm by proportion, in a timber frame with cream mat. Small paper ticket at top of mat (Armitage lot ticket).
lots.condition: Colours look fresh in the photos, no obvious foxing, staining or fading visible through the glass; frame shows normal wear. Backing tissue present.
lots.question_for_armitage: What is the image size, and is there any foxing, fading or water staining on the sheet? Is there a title or date on the back (for example a gallery label naming the church)?

No artist name on the label; attribution to Ryllton Viney rests on the catalogue, supported by the same 2012 Provence theme as lot 1006, which is labelled Viney.

Photo 1: large stretched canvas, unframed, roughly 1 m high by eye; columns and plinths in grey and white, peach band, dark blue textured band, collage-like layers.
